title: A familiar name returns to lead ICE amid renewed political pressure
summary: A longtime DHS official with prior ties to Obama-era immigration enforcement and private detention work is stepping back into a top role at a pivotal moment for the agency.

title: ‘Sermonizing’ Easter email prompts USDA employees to sue agency
summary: In response to the lawsuit, the department said, “we will keep the plaintiffs in our prayers.”

title: House GOP probes agency settlements with federal workers
summary: Republican members of the House Oversight and Reform Committee argued agencies should settle less often with feds who allege prohibited personnel practices, but experts say the government acts similarly to private sector litigants.

title: $1 billion Secret Service funding boost plan draws scrutiny over limited details
summary: Lawmakers are seeking a clearer breakdown of how the funds would be used as debate continues over security upgrades, modernization projects and the scale of the request.

title: Hegseth rethinking Army reforms, cuts to aviation
summary: One year after launching the Army Transformation Initiative, the Defense secretary says he's reviewing the to-do list.

title: DOT inspector general reviewing complaint against Sean Duffy over reality show
summary: Ethics watchdogs have concerns about the cabinet secretary's forthcoming travel show.

title: Watchdog recommends nearly 100 ways for agencies to save tens of billions
summary: Agencies have implemented a majority of previous Government Accountability Office recommendations regarding duplicative federal programs, generating almost $775 billion in financial benefits.

title: ‘It would be insane’ for spy agencies to not have AI model early access, lawmaker says
summary: The top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee said the Commerce Department should also have a role in AI policy.

title: Trump taps former FEMA official ousted after defending agency
summary: Cameron Hamilton, who was removed after publicly opposing efforts to eliminate FEMA, would return to lead the agency as the administration pushes states to take on a larger disaster response role.

title: Federal discipline was never supposed to be punitive. The MSPB appeal framework reflects that
summary: COMMENTARY | Forget what you think you know about federal employee discipline. The MSPB's penalty review is not focused on the severity of the misconduct. It's focused on one thing: can the employee be fixed?

title: Army small business office pulls the plug on LinkedIn posts
summary: The office directs followers to its website, but critics say the move cuts off a key connection to the defense industrial base.

title: The Army wants to reinvent how it feeds soldiers in the field
summary: A new sources sought notice targets alternative protein technologies as a means to reduce logistics burdens and strengthen supply chain resilience.

title: Anthropic, Code for America pilot AI tools for SNAP eligibility support
summary: The effort is aimed at helping eligibility staff interpret complex federal rules and manage increasing administrative demands tied to SNAP policy changes.

title: The number of feds in tax debt spiked during the pandemic
summary: Around 215,000 federal employees are behind on their tax bills, IG finds.

title: ‘This will cost lives’: Researchers slam Trump cuts to addiction programs and staffing
summary: The Addiction Science Defense Network in a new report criticized several reforms at the Health and Human Services Department, including the elimination of a program that collected information on hospital visits across the country related to substance use trends.

title: CBP backs off border wall construction plans in Big Bend National Park
summary: The agency says it will use surveillance technology and infrastructure upgrades in the park after bipartisan opposition to the proposed wall project.

title: Pentagon will ‘never again’ rely on a single AI provider, official says
summary: Defense Under Secretary for Research and Engineering Emil Michael said new agreements with Big Tech companies are a “counterstatement” to the ongoing Anthropic-Pentagon conflict as the agency prioritizes flexible contracts.

title: A USDA cow scientist won an award for helping dairy farmers produce more milk. He’s worried about the future of government research under Trump
summary: The Partnership for Public Service, which runs an annual awards program for federal employees, recognized fewer civil servants this year as a result of fewer agencies participating.

title: Feds wary of skills-based hiring survey after 15 months of attacks
summary: The combination of a lack of outreach around a newly deployed survey of federal workers’ skillsets with the recent flood of layoffs, purges and reorganizations has made some reluctant to participate in the bipartisan initiative.

title: Inside the effort to connect Congress with the feds enacting its policies
summary: Those writing laws don’t often hear from those charged with implementing them. The POPVOX Foundation wants that to change.

title: FEMA should employ fewer staff and offer aid to fewer individuals, Trump’s council recommends
summary: The changes come after the president proposed an overhaul, or outright elimination, of the disaster response agency.

title: A week of recognition, and a career of service
summary: Behind the honors and milestones, federal employees carry a lasting sense of purpose that extends well beyond a single week.

title: ‘Highly problematic for a thousand reasons’: NIH employees criticize Trump-era requirement to scrutinize grants with words related to diversity
summary: One staffer said that officials are employing more systematic methods to pinpoint NIH-funded research that the administration may object to, but that the additional reviews are time-consuming and lack transparency.
